propositions: A contributor-posted `recheck-review` comment on a change with a current-revision coverage-gap -1 (any sub-reason: llm-unavailable, review-error, scanner, indeterminate, gate-disabled, or retries-exhausted escalation) resets the per-revision retry budget, enqueues a forced re-review via the existing _rebar_force path, and posts a queued-reply comment with no vote labels.

A `recheck-review` comment on a change whose current-revision LLM-Review verdict is a finding-BLOCK (`[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]` or its merge form) is refused: no enqueue, no budget reset, no vote change; a refusal reply is posted and RETRIGGER_REFUSED is logged.

The retrigger eligibility decision reads the bot's authoritative current-revision LLM-Review vote message tag from Gerrit (via GET /a/changes/{id}/messages), parses the tag by stem (stripping trailing merge-change suffix), and classifies all three production tag shapes (_TAG_SUFFIXES vocabulary, hardcoded merge-review literal, and in-tag merge-change variants).

The Gerrit webhook config gains `event = comment-added` subscription and the worker routes comment-added payloads to retrigger.handle_comment_added() instead of review_and_vote, with bot-authored comments and non-matching tokens silently skipped.

The retrigger reply uses POST /a/changes/{id}/revisions/{rev}/review with a message-only JSON body (no `labels` key) to guarantee no vote displacement, and the /rerun operator endpoint also resets the attempts budget before enqueueing to harmonize retry semantics with 0347.

Unparseable or absent vote tags are treated as eligible (fail-open to a fresh fail-closed review), and the contributor trigger mechanism is bounded by the eligibility gate refusing only real findings, not by an artificial numeric retry cap.
